markets.review: B2C imported software/digital supplies. Verify Australian-consumer status and relevant external-territory exceptions.
Remote software/digital supplies to New Zealand consumers; exclude supplies treated under B2B rules.
Authority explicitly lists software access and downloads. Norway VAT area only, not Svalbard or Jan Mayen.
9% from 2024-01-01. OVR B2C remote services; registered-business treatment and threshold assessment separate.

markets.authority: United Arab Emirates Federal Tax Authority
markets.review: Electronic-service use/enjoyment and nonresident registration review required; not a general rule for all special supplies.
8% from 2024-03-01; digital-service guide includes software subscriptions. Assess exemptions and transitional payment rules separately.
RR 3-2025 digital-service rate. Nonresident B2C supplier collection differs from B2B buyer withholding.
15%, not withdrawn proposed 15.5%/16% increases. Registration thresholds changed in 2026; do not infer registration from old guidance.
Authority expressly includes software under remote services. B2C simplified regime and actual seller status require review.
Standard rate candidate for software, not reduced-rate books or media. VOES and B2B treatment require separate review.
16% digital-supply VAT. Older FAQ income-tax/DST discussion is not authority for current income taxes; do not add DST to checkout.

The 10% standard rate includes 7.8% national and 2.2% local consumption tax. Electronic services supplied to recipients with a Japanese address are domestic in principle; food/newspaper reduced rates do not describe software. B2B reverse-charge and platform rules require separate treatment.

markets.authority: Argentina Agencia de Recaudación y Control Aduanero
markets.review: ARCA classifies software, downloads and SaaS as digital services; its published dialogue identifies the applicable IVA as 21%. The payment-intermediary collection mechanism and provincial turnover taxes are outside this single national IVA rule.

markets.authority: Colombia Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
markets.review: DIAN states that services supplied from abroad are within IVA and the general rate is 19% unless an explicit exclusion or differential rate applies. The separate card-withholding option and provider filing status require operational review.

7% VAT on electronic services supplied by nonresident operators to non-VAT-registered Thai customers. The THB 1.8 million annual registration threshold and customer VAT status remain separate controls.

markets.authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance Taxation Administration
markets.review: 5% business tax for offshore electronic-services entities selling to domestic individuals. Registration threshold, evidence of customer location, and intermediary status require separate review.

20% general KDV candidate for electronic services sold by a nonresident to non-KDV-registered individuals. Türkiye's separate digital-services tax is seller-level and is not added to checkout by this rule.

markets.authority: Saudi Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority
markets.review: 15% standard VAT candidate for taxable electronic services supplied to a Saudi consumer. Customer residence evidence, marketplace responsibility and registration status remain separate controls.

20% VAT is added to taxable electronic services supplied by a nonresident to individuals, except exempt operations. Customer VAT status, the registration threshold and statutory exemptions remain separate controls.

13% IVA on the gross value of cross-border digital services and intangible goods, including software. Voluntary supplier registration versus card-issuer withholding must be resolved operationally to prevent double collection.

The authority explicitly includes computer software, digital applications and subscriptions. The current statutory 12% rate applies to a deemed base of 11/12 of the pre-VAT payment, producing an 11% checkout amount. Only an appointed PMSE collector may collect; appointment, customer-location evidence and filing remain separate controls.

Article 23 sets the 20% general VAT rate, while Article 12 places electronically supplied services at the recipient's residence or domicile. Foreign-supplier registration, consumer evidence and any reverse-charge boundary remain separate activation controls.

The 2026 Tax Code raises the base VAT rate to 16%. The State Revenue Committee separately confirms VAT administration and conditional registration for foreign internet platforms supplying digital services. Registration status, customer location and exceptions remain separate controls.

The 2026 combined IGV/IPM rate is 18%. SUNAT states that nonresidents providing digital services or online intangible goods to non-business consumers must register. Registration status, customer evidence and exclusions remain separate activation controls.

Sections 148 and 151 of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 set VAT at 7.5%, require a nonresident making taxable supplies to Nigeria to register and invoice VAT, and permit the Revenue Service to appoint a nonresident supplier to collect. Actual appointment, customer status, invoice requirements and exempt supplies remain separate activation controls.

Finance Circular 735 uses a downloaded mobile application as an in-scope remotely supplied service and requires a nonresident supplying dematerialized remote services to non-taxable Moroccan customers to register, declare and pay VAT. The standard 20% rate applies unless a specific reduction or exemption does; registration and classification approval remain separate activation controls.

The authority's nonresident remote-services guide expressly includes online games, apps, software and software maintenance. The general 14% VAT applies to taxable B2C supplies; the EGP 500,000 registration threshold, customer status, exemptions and B2B reverse charge remain separate activation controls.

The authority states that the current IVA rate for digital services is 15% and provides a voluntary registration route for nonresident digital-service providers to collect it. Provider registration versus payment-intermediary withholding, customer status, evidence and specific zero-rated services remain separate activation controls.

Electronic-only downloaded software guidance describes nontaxable sales; do not apply to all delivery models. Recheck 2026 legislation and future-effective changes before an exemption candidate.
Federal GST/HST is province-specific. BC/SK/MB PST and Quebec QST are separate; no Canada-wide total.
No VAT/sales-tax regime requires explicit non-collection semantics, not fabricated registration or treating absent data as zero.
12.5% standard rate from 2025-08-01. Imported software/nonresident collection versus recipient responsibility remains unresolved; rate alone cannot activate checkout tax.
